title: Chess, But One of My Pawns is Secretly a Queen
summary: Secret Queen chess played online (third-party site with chat, blue clocks) against ~1400-1600 rated humans (e.g. a 1415 opponent, oessamelsayed1 1613). Before the game each player secretly chooses one of their own pawns to be a secret queen: it looks like a pawn but may move like a queen (and still like a pawn). The opponent does not know which pawn it is until it moves like a queen. Second episode of the series; goal is to win three games (placeholder rating 1600). Blitz clocks (~3 min).
rules: Standard starting position, normal chess rules, blitz clock.
At the start each player secretly selects one of their eight pawns as the Secret Queen (marked with a star badge only on its owner's screen).
The secret queen is revealed when it gives check, when it promotes, or when it moves in a way a pawn cannot (per episode 1, I_TbJqRHtf4 01:43).
Capturing an unrevealed secret-queen pawn removes it like any pawn.
The opponent's secret queen is unknown; any of their pawns might be it.
win_condition: Checkmate (or flag/resign) the opponent; goal: win three games.

opponent.name: Online humans ~1400-1600 (e.g. 1415-rated opponent, oessamelsayed1 1613)

current_impl_issues: Legacy 'secretq': one of your pawns (gold outline) can move like a queen - only the player has one. Real: BOTH sides have a secret queen pawn, chosen by each player; the bot's should be hidden and chosen at random/strategically; player should pick their own pawn. Opponent should be ~1500 human-level, not Stockfish.
